```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD, INN lysergide) is a serotonin 5-HT2A agonist
psychedelic. Dolder 2017 analysed plasma LSD, three subjective-effect visual
analog scales (VAS) and four vital signs from two placebo-controlled,
double-blind crossover studies at the University Hospital Basel, in which
healthy adults took a single oral dose of 100 ug (Study 1) or 200 ug (Study 2)
LSD.

The analysis is a **two-stage** one: every subject was fitted on their own in
Phoenix WinNonlin, first with a one-compartment PK model (first-order
absorption, no lag time, first-order elimination) and then, with the predicted
concentrations held fixed, with an effect-compartment sigmoid-Emax PK-PD link
model (Supplementary Figure S1). The paper reports summary statistics of the
individual estimates (geometric means for PK, Table 1; arithmetic means for PD,
Table 2), separately for each dose, not a population model. The PD model was
fitted to each of seven endpoints separately, so the paper contributes eight
model files; the covariate `DOSE_HIGH` selects the 100 ug (0) or the 200 ug (1)
row of Tables 1 and 2.

```{r models}
endpoints <- c(
  Dolder_2017_lysergide_anydrugeffect = "anydrugeffectvas",
  Dolder_2017_lysergide_gooddrugeffect = "gooddrugeffectvas",
  Dolder_2017_lysergide_baddrugeffect = "baddrugeffectvas",
  Dolder_2017_lysergide_hr = "hrcfb",
  Dolder_2017_lysergide_bodytemp = "bodytempcfb",
  Dolder_2017_lysergide_dbp = "dbpcfb",
  Dolder_2017_lysergide_sbp = "sbpcfb"
)
endpoint_label <- c(
  anydrugeffectvas = "Any drug effect (%)",
  gooddrugeffectvas = "Good drug effect (%)",
  baddrugeffectvas = "Bad drug effect (%)",
  hrcfb = "Heart rate (beats/min)",
  bodytempcfb = "Body temperature (deg C)",
  dbpcfb = "Diastolic BP (mmHg)",
  sbpcfb = "Systolic BP (mmHg)"
)
lsd_models <- c("Dolder_2017_lysergide", names(endpoints))
mods <- lapply(stats::setNames(lsd_models, lsd_models), function(m) {
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))
})
```

* Citation: `r mods[[1]]$reference`
* Article: [Clin Pharmacokinet 2017;56:1219-1230](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-017-0513-9) (open access)
* Supplement: Electronic Supplementary Material 1 (model schematic, individual
  fits and diagnostic plots; no additional parameter tables)

```{r description}
cat(strwrap(mods[["Dolder_2017_lysergide"]]$description, 76), sep = "\n")
```

# Population

Forty healthy adults took part (Methods, Participants). Study 1 (100 ug,
NCT02308969): 24 subjects, 12 men and 12 women, age 33 +/- 11 years (25-60),
weight 68 +/- 8 kg (55-85). Study 2 (200 ug, NCT01878942): 16 subjects, 8 men
and 8 women, age 29 +/- 6 years (25-51), weight 72 +/- 12 kg (52-98). Eleven had
used a hallucinogen before. Each study crossed LSD over with placebo, and every
pharmacodynamic effect is the difference from placebo in the same subject at
the same time point.

```{r population}
str(mods[["Dolder_2017_lysergide"]]$population)
```

# Source trace

Each `ini()` value carries its source location as an in-file comment. The PK
layer is identical in all eight files.

| Parameter / equation | 100 ug (`DOSE_HIGH = 0`) | 200 ug (`DOSE_HIGH = 1`) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lka` / `lka_highdose` (k01) | 1.4 1/h | 1.2 1/h | Table 1 geometric mean |
| `lcl` / `lcl_highdose` (CL/F) | 12.3 L/h | 9.9 L/h | Table 1 geometric mean |
| `lvc` / `lvc_highdose` (Vd) | 46 L | 37 L | Table 1 geometric mean |
| `emax`, `lec50`, `lhill`, `lke0` (each endpoint) | see below | see below | Table 2 mean of individual estimates |
| `propSd`, `addSd_<endpoint>` | 0 (fixed) | 0 (fixed) | not reported |
| One compartment, first-order absorption, no lag | n/a | n/a | Methods 'PK Analyses and PK-PD Modeling' |
| `d/dt(effect) <- ke0 * (Cc - effect)`; `E = Emax Ce^gamma / (EC50^gamma + Ce^gamma)` | n/a | n/a | Methods; Supplementary Figure S1 |
| Effect = drug minus placebo at the same time point (zero baseline) | n/a | n/a | Methods 'Statistical Analyses' |

```{r pd-trace}
pd_names <- c("emax", "lec50", "lhill", "lke0")
pd_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(endpoints), function(m) {
  th <- mods[[m]]$theta
  data.frame(
    endpoint = endpoint_label[[endpoints[[m]]]],
    dose = c("100 ug", "200 ug"),
    Emax = c(th[["emax"]], th[["emax_highdose"]]),
    EC50 = exp(c(th[["lec50"]], th[["lec50_highdose"]])),
    gamma = exp(c(th[["lhill"]], th[["lhill_highdose"]])),
    ke0 = exp(c(th[["lke0"]], th[["lke0_highdose"]]))
  )
}))
pd_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint, "Dose" = dose, "Emax" = Emax,
    "EC50 (ng/mL)" = EC50, "gamma" = gamma, "ke0 (1/h)" = ke0
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PD parameters as packaged (Table 2 means).")
```

The PK layer is the same in every file:

```{r pk-identical}
pk_names <- c("lka", "lka_highdose", "lcl", "lcl_highdose", "lvc", "lvc_highdose")
pk_vals <- sapply(mods, function(m) m$theta[pk_names])
stopifnot(all(abs(pk_vals - pk_vals[, 1]) < 1e-12))
exp(pk_vals[, 1])
```

# Dosing

Doses are entered in ug of LSD as administered (d-lysergic acid diethylamide
hydrate capsules, 100 or 200 ug), and plasma concentrations are in ng/mL. The
Table 1 identity AUC = Dose / (CL/F) holds with the nominal doses
(100 / 12.3 = 8.1 and 200 / 9.9 = 20.2 ng*h/mL against 8.1 and 20.3), so the
nominal dose is the one the analysis used.

```{r doses}
doses <- data.frame(
  dose_group = c("100 ug", "200 ug"),
  id = 1:2,
  amt = c(100, 200),
  DOSE_HIGH = c(0L, 1L)
)

times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 60), seq(1, 24, by = 1 / 12))))

# Observation rows sit on the `central` state with dvid = 1: the PK-PD files
# have two outputs (Cc and the effect), and rxode2 returns both at every
# observation row.
make_events <- function(cmt_dose = "depot") {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(doses)), function(i) {
    d <- doses[i, ]
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      data.frame(id = d$id, time = 0, amt = d$amt, evid = 1L, cmt = cmt_dose, dvid = NA_integer_),
      data.frame(id = d$id, time = times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
    ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(DOSE_HIGH = d$DOSE_HIGH)
  }))
}
ev_oral <- make_events("depot")

# The models have no between-subject variability, so rxode2's warning about a
# multi-subject solve without omega is expected and muffled here only.
solve_model <- function(m, ev = ev_oral) {
  s <- withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[m]], ev, keep = "DOSE_HIGH"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
  as.data.frame(s) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose_group = doses$dose_group[match(id, doses$id)])
}
```

# Pharmacokinetics

## Closed-form checks

For a one-compartment model with first-order absorption, AUC = Dose / CL and
t1/2 = ln 2 / (CL / V) exactly. Table 1 reports both, so a transcription error
in CL/F, Vd or the dose units shows here directly.

```{r closed-form}
p <- exp(pk_vals[, 1])
cf <- data.frame(
  dose_group = doses$dose_group,
  cl = c(p[["lcl"]], p[["lcl_highdose"]]),
  vc = c(p[["lvc"]], p[["lvc_highdose"]]),
  ka = c(p[["lka"]], p[["lka_highdose"]])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    kel = cl / vc,
    auc = doses$amt / cl,
    half.life = log(2) / kel,
    tmax = log(ka / kel) / (ka - kel)
  )
cf
# Table 1: lambda 0.27 1/h, t1/2 2.6 h, AUCinf 8.1 and 20.3 ng*h/mL.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(cf$kel - 0.27) < 0.005),
  all(abs(cf$half.life - 2.6) < 0.05),
  abs(cf$auc[1] / 8.1 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(cf$auc[2] / 20.3 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

## PKNCA against Table 1

```{r pknca}
sim_pk <- solve_model("Dolder_2017_lysergide")

conc <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dose_group)
conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc,
  conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, dose_group) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, dose_group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)
dose_df <- doses |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | dose_group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | dose_group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

tab1 <- data.frame(
  dose_group = c("100 ug", "200 ug"),
  cmax = c(1.3, 3.1),
  tmax = c(1.4, 1.5),
  aucinf.obs = c(8.1, 20.3),
  half.life = c(2.6, 2.6)
)
cmp_pk <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca,
  reference = tab1,
  by = "dose_group",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "h*ng/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_pk,
  caption = paste(
    "Typical-value model vs Table 1 geometric means of the individual",
    "compartmental estimates. * differs from the reference by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

```{r pknca-gate}
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(dose_group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(tab1, -dose_group, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("dose_group", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / ref - 1))
nca_df
# AUC and t1/2 are exact functions of CL/F and Vd. Cmax and tmax depend on
# k01, whose geometric mean does not commute with the Cmax / tmax formulas,
# and the Table 1 values are geometric means of the individual Cmax / tmax.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_df$pct_diff[nca_df$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"]) < 2),
  all(abs(nca_df$pct_diff[nca_df$PPTESTCD == "half.life"]) < 3),
  all(abs(nca_df$pct_diff[nca_df$PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax")]) < 20)
)
```

The typical-value Cmax is about 13% above the Table 1 geometric mean at both
doses (1.47 vs 1.3 and 3.5 vs 3.1 ng/mL). That is the expected gap between the
curve at the geometric-mean parameters and the geometric mean of individual
Cmax values: k01 varies more than ten-fold between subjects (0.27-10 1/h), and
Cmax is concave in k01, so averaging individual Cmax values gives less than
the Cmax of the averaged k01.

## Concentration-time profiles (Figure 1a)

```{r fig1a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1a of Dolder 2017: plasma LSD after 100 and 200 ug orally, typical-value model. The published panel shows the mean +/- SEM of the observed concentrations."}
ggplot(sim_pk, aes(time, Cc, colour = dose_group)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "LSD (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Pharmacodynamics

```{r pd-solve}
sim_pd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(endpoints), function(m) {
  s <- solve_model(m)
  data.frame(
    id = s$id, time = s$time, Cc = s$Cc, Ce = s$effect,
    value = s[[endpoints[[m]]]], endpoint = endpoints[[m]],
    dose_group = s$dose_group
  )
}))
```

## Effect-time curves (Figures 1b, d, f and 2a, c, e, g)

```{r fig-effects, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "Replicates the effect-time panels of Figures 1 and 2 of Dolder 2017: typical-value predicted effect (difference from placebo) by dose. The published panels show the mean +/- SEM of the observed effects."}
sim_pd |>
  dplyr::mutate(endpoint = factor(endpoint_label[endpoint], levels = endpoint_label)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = dose_group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Effect (difference from placebo)", colour = "Dose") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Hysteresis (Figure 1c)

```{r fig1c, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1c of Dolder 2017: 'any drug effect' against plasma LSD, typical-value model. The loop runs counterclockwise because the effect site lags plasma (ke0 1.8 and 3.4 1/h)."}
sim_pd |>
  dplyr::filter(endpoint == "anydrugeffectvas") |>
  ggplot(aes(Cc, value, colour = dose_group)) +
  geom_path() +
  labs(x = "LSD (ng/mL)", y = "Any drug effect (%)", colour = "Dose") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Effect onset, peak and offset ('any drug effect')

Dolder 2017 derived onset, offset, duration and time to peak from each
subject's model-predicted 'any drug effect' curve, with a threshold of 10% of
the maximal possible effect (10 VAS points), and reported their means (Results,
Pharmacodynamics). The same quantities for the typical curve:

```{r effect-metrics}
any_metrics <- sim_pd |>
  dplyr::filter(endpoint == "anydrugeffectvas") |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Emax_pred = max(value),
    tmaxE = time[which.max(value)],
    onset = min(time[value >= 10]),
    offset = max(time[value >= 10]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(duration = offset - onset)

ref_metrics <- data.frame(
  dose_group = c("100 ug", "200 ug"),
  onset_ref = c(0.8, 0.4),
  tmaxE_ref = c(2.8, 2.5),
  offset_ref = c(9.0, 11.6),
  duration_ref = c(8.2, 11.2)
)
any_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(any_metrics, ref_metrics, by = "dose_group")
any_cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    dose_group,
    Emax_pred = round(Emax_pred),
    onset = round(onset, 2), onset_ref,
    tmaxE = round(tmaxE, 2), tmaxE_ref,
    offset = round(offset, 1), offset_ref,
    duration = round(duration, 1), duration_ref
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose" = dose_group, "Peak effect, typical (%)" = Emax_pred,
    "Onset, typical (h)" = onset, "Onset, paper (h)" = onset_ref,
    "Peak time, typical (h)" = tmaxE, "Peak time, paper (h)" = tmaxE_ref,
    "Offset, typical (h)" = offset, "Offset, paper (h)" = offset_ref,
    "Duration, typical (h)" = duration, "Duration, paper (h)" = duration_ref
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Typical-value 'any drug effect' curve vs the means of the individual",
    "predicted curves (Results, Pharmacodynamics)."
  ))
```

The typical curve is one curve at the average parameters, whereas the paper
reports means of 24 or 16 individual curves, so the two agree in shape and
order of magnitude rather than exactly. The typical curve starts and peaks
about half an hour earlier than the published means and ends about 2 h
earlier, so its duration is about 20% shorter (6.7 vs 8.2 h at 100 ug, 8.9 vs
11.2 h at 200 ug). A mean of individual curves is wider than the curve at the
mean parameters: subjects with slow absorption or elimination, or a low
EC50, stay above the 10-point threshold for longer, which pulls the mean
offset and duration up. The checks below test what the typical curve must
reproduce: an effect onset within the first hour, a peak delayed behind the
plasma peak by the effect-site equilibration and within 1 h of the published
mean, a longer effect after 200 ug than after 100 ug, and a duration within
35% of the published mean.

```{r effect-gates}
tmax_pk <- cf$tmax
stopifnot(
  all(any_cmp$onset < 1),
  all(any_cmp$tmaxE > tmax_pk),
  all(abs(any_cmp$tmaxE - any_cmp$tmaxE_ref) < 1),
  any_cmp$duration[2] > any_cmp$duration[1],
  all(abs(any_cmp$duration / any_cmp$duration_ref - 1) < 0.35),
  all(any_cmp$Emax_pred > 70)
)
```

## Predicted effect peak after intravenous dosing (Discussion)

The Discussion uses lambda and ke0 to predict the time of the peak 'any drug
effect' after an intravenous bolus: about 70 min with the 100 ug parameters and
50 min with the 200 ug parameters. After a bolus the effect-site concentration,
and so the effect, peaks at ln(ke0 / lambda) / (ke0 - lambda). Dosing the same
amounts into `central` must reproduce this, which checks lambda (through CL/F
and Vd) and ke0 together.

```{r iv-check}
sim_iv <- solve_model("Dolder_2017_lysergide_anydrugeffect", make_events("central"))
iv <- sim_iv |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tmax_effect_min = 60 * time[which.max(anydrugeffectvas)], .groups = "drop")
th <- mods[["Dolder_2017_lysergide_anydrugeffect"]]$theta
ke0 <- exp(c(th[["lke0"]], th[["lke0_highdose"]]))
iv$closed_form_min <- 60 * log(ke0 / cf$kel) / (ke0 - cf$kel)
iv$discussion_min <- c(70, 50)
iv
stopifnot(
  all(abs(iv$tmax_effect_min - iv$closed_form_min) < 1.5),
  all(abs(iv$tmax_effect_min - iv$discussion_min) < 6)
)
```

## Peak effects of the vital signs

Figure 2 shows that LSD raised blood pressure, heart rate and body temperature
to similar extents at both doses. The typical-value peaks:

```{r vital-peaks}
sim_pd |>
  dplyr::group_by(endpoint, dose_group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(peak = max(value), tpeak = time[which.max(value)], .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(endpoint = endpoint_label[endpoint]) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = dose_group, values_from = c(peak, tpeak)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint,
    "Peak, 100 ug" = `peak_100 ug`, "Peak, 200 ug" = `peak_200 ug`,
    "Peak time, 100 ug (h)" = `tpeak_100 ug`, "Peak time, 200 ug (h)" = `tpeak_200 ug`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value peak effects (difference from placebo).")
```

```{r temp-gate}
# Body temperature equilibrates most slowly (Table 2 t1/2 ke0 107 and 136 min
# against 13-53 min for the cardiovascular effects), so its typical peak must
# come last among the vital signs at each dose.
tpk <- sim_pd |>
  dplyr::filter(endpoint %in% c("hrcfb", "bodytempcfb", "dbpcfb", "sbpcfb")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(endpoint, dose_group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tpeak = time[which.max(value)], .groups = "drop")
for (dg in doses$dose_group) {
  x <- tpk[tpk$dose_group == dg, ]
  stopifnot(x$tpeak[x$endpoint == "bodytempcfb"] == max(x$tpeak))
}
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two-stage source, typical values only.** Dolder 2017 fitted each subject
  individually and reported summaries of the individual estimates, so the
  models carry no between-subject variability. PK parameters are the Table 1
  geometric means and PD parameters the Table 2 arithmetic means. The 95%
  confidence intervals, ranges and standard deviations of the individual
  estimates were not converted into between-subject variances: an
  individual-fit spread mixes true variability with estimation error and is
  not a population-model omega. Combining a mean PD parameter set with the
  geometric-mean PK gives a typical curve, which differs systematically from
  the mean of individual curves the paper plots, as the tables above show.
* **Per-dose parameter sets.** The paper gives no pooled estimate; each dose
  was a separate study in different participants, with plasma LSD measured in
  different laboratories (Discussion, limitations). `DOSE_HIGH` therefore
  selects the published row for each dose. The authors concluded the PK is
  dose proportional; the differences between the two PK rows (CL/F 12.3 vs
  9.9 L/h, Vd 46 vs 37 L) are within the overlap of their confidence intervals
  and are not a modelled dose effect. Other doses should not be simulated by
  interpolating `DOSE_HIGH`.
* **Responder subsets.** 'Bad drug effect' could not be estimated in subjects
  who never rated it above 5% (8 of 24 at 100 ug, 5 of 16 at 200 ug), and each
  vital sign in one to three subjects whose values did not change enough, so
  those parameter means describe responders.
* **Emax limits.** The fits bounded Emax to 0-100% for the VAS and to at most
  100 beats/min, 2 deg C, 50 mmHg (diastolic) and 80 mmHg (systolic) for the
  vital signs. The typical values lie inside these limits; the models do not
  impose them.
* **Residual errors fixed at zero.** The paper does not describe the residual
  error models or report their magnitudes; `propSd` (PK) and
  `addSd_<endpoint>` (PD) are fixed at 0 placeholders.
* **Effects are placebo-corrected.** Every PD endpoint is the value after LSD
  minus the value after placebo in the same subject at the same time, so each
  model has zero baseline. The vital-sign outputs are named with the library's
  change-score suffix (`hrcfb`, `dbpcfb`, `sbpcfb`, `bodytempcfb`); here the
  change is from the time-matched placebo value, not from a pre-dose baseline.
* **Dose units.** Doses are ug of LSD as given in the capsules (nominally 100
  and 200 ug of d-lysergic acid diethylamide hydrate); Table 1 AUC equals the
  nominal dose divided by CL/F.
